correctness.rationale: The source next-generation matrix and bite partition give exactly R_FA=A x², R_FH=B(1−x)², R_CH=C and the stated larger-root quadratic. For 0≤x<1 and B,C>0 the larger root is simple and exceeds C. An interior critical point must satisfy y=Ax and x=(B+C)/(A+B); sign of y’ at x=0 and near x=1 proves the full unique-minimizer classification with all endpoint cases. The example uses positive b, populations, recovery/death and probabilities in (0,1]; an exact rational identity shows P(1,x(p))=(6−80(p−1/2)²)/(25(5−4p)²). Its lower quadratic root lies below 3/5<1, so the sign gives the complete subcritical interval. Standalone exact rational and random-sample checker returned VERIFY_OK. Tests do not replace the analytic universal proof.

value.rationale: The source uses human urban-residence fraction p as a biologically interpretable variable and a three-cycle infection network. The exact three-regime minimizing residence rule and sharp synthetic threshold window resolve whether partially moving humans to the city can lower the four-population invasion threshold, an outcome not settled by source R0 bounds or fitted sensitivities. The distinctive fixed city loop creates the sharp A>C feasibility criterion and clarifies that fully urban human separation can leave wildlife infection active. This is a natural complete parameter classification with explicit mathematical and interpretation value, not an arbitrary slice or a claim about clinical intervention outcomes.
